Options & Call-Convexity Playbook (LNG)

BULL CALL DEBIT SPREAD — Buy 1x LNG 2027-01-15 $300/$350 Bull Call Spread (63 DTE) at $16.85 net debit ($1,685.00 max loss -> $3,315.00 max profit, 1.97:1 R:R).

Multi-Timeframe Chart Context (1W / 1D / 4H): In Stage 2 uptrend, but extended above 50D SMA (284.43); chasing short-dated calls carries pullback risk. Account / Chain Feed: No open Robinhood tab in Chrome; live account quotes skipped, using public options chain.

Beginner Guide: How This Call Trade Works in Plain Dollars

Why this spread works differently from buying shares: Selling the upper $350 call collects $4.05/sh upfront, lowering your breakeven to $316.85 and protecting you against post-news volatility crush.

Exact wallet math (1 contract = 100 shares): You buy the $300 Call for $20.90 and simultaneously sell the $350 Call for $4.05, paying $16.85/sh net ($1,685.00 total for 1 spread(s)). That $1,685.00 is the absolute maximum you can lose.

Breakeven & profit ceiling: At expiry (2027-01-15), you start making money above $316.85 (+3.1% from $307.44). Anywhere at or above $350, your $1,685.00 turns into $5,000.00 (+$3,315.00 net profit).

Speed & time decay in plain English: Today, each $1 move up in LNG adds ~$40.00 to your spread (Net Delta), while sitting flat costs ~$5.32/day in time decay (Net Theta) — much lower than an unhedged call because the sold $350 call decays in your favor.
